sentenceSets.sentence: His grandstanding during the hearing impressed television viewers but irritated colleagues who had come for information.

answerChoices.reasoning: Eloquence would win over the room as well as the cameras, whereas this behavior splits the two audiences by delighting viewers and annoying the people in attendance.
Bluster is empty noise and bullying, which would be unlikely to impress the viewers at home the sentence says were won over.
Candor supplies frank information, the very thing the irritated colleagues had come for and did not get.
Persistence would mean pressing a line of questioning doggedly, which serves the colleagues' purpose rather than frustrating it.
Expertise would satisfy those who came for information instead of irritating them.
Brevity would leave more of the hearing for substance, which is what the colleagues wanted.
Arriving on time is a courtesy that would not impress television viewers or annoy anyone.
Being well prepared would help the informational purpose the colleagues came for.
Silence could not impress television viewers in the way the sentence describes.
Modesty draws no cameras and would not divide the two audiences at all.
Diligence is steady hard work, which the colleagues seeking information would have welcomed.

sentenceSets.sentence: Rain drove the crowd under the grandstand, where the noise of forty thousand feet drowned out the announcer.

answerChoices.reasoning: A canopy is a stretched cover with nothing underneath it, so it could not have the pounding floor overhead that the noise of thousands of feet implies.
An awning shelters a doorway or window and is far too small to take a crowd of forty thousand.
A scoreboard is a display panel and offers no covered space for spectators to shelter in.
A dugout is a small bench area for players, not a structure that could hold an entire stadium crowd.
A turnstile is a gate that admits people one at a time and provides no shelter at all.
The infield is open ground in the middle of the track, exposed to exactly the rain the crowd is escaping.
A podium is a small raised platform for one or two people and has no underside to shelter a crowd.
A marquee is a sign or a tent at an entrance, not the seating structure implied by feet overhead.
A runway is a paved strip for aircraft and is not part of a stadium or a shelter from rain.
An orchestra is a group of musicians and cannot be something a crowd takes cover beneath.
A referee is a person and offers no shelter to forty thousand spectators.

sentenceSets.sentence: Do not grandstand at the settlement conference; the mediator has heard every speech twice and wants numbers.

answerChoices.reasoning: Improvising means working without preparation, but the warning is aimed at speeches the mediator has already heard, which points to performing for effect rather than speaking off the cuff.
Equivocating hedges to avoid commitment, while the behavior being discouraged is the delivery of familiar oratory in place of figures.
Conceding gives ground to the other side, which no one would warn against in the same breath as asking for numbers.
Interrupting is a discourtesy about timing, whereas the mediator's complaint is about set speeches that substitute for concrete proposals.
Preparing would help produce the numbers the mediator wants rather than waste the session.
Listening is welcome in a mediation and would not be the subject of a warning.
Arriving is a prerequisite for taking part and is not a behavior anyone would caution against.
Negotiating is the whole purpose of a settlement conference, so it cannot be the thing to avoid.
An apology is brief and would not be mistaken for the speeches the mediator has heard twice.
Whispering is the opposite of the conspicuous performance the mediator is tired of.
Compromise moves toward the numbers the mediator is asking for, not away from them.
